correctness.rationale: For \(n=4r+2\), translating an odd five-cycle and summing edge incidences gives \(n\le2f-e_i\). Both inner rings have odd length \(n/2\), so \(e_i\ge2\), hence \(f\ge n/2+1\) and energy at least \(-2(n-1)J\). The finite eight-state transfer counts every labelled assignment once. Its exact determinant-trace identity gives ground-state count \(2m^2F_m\). A spin-fugacity refinement has normalized determinant \(E_0=(1-3Y^2+Y^4)^2\) and the next odd coefficient \(-2Y^7+(2-w^2-w^{-2})Y^5-2Y\), which forces magnetization \(M\in\{0,\pm4\}\) and determines each nonzero-magnetization multiplicity as \(m[t^{(m-5)/2}](1-3t+t^2)^{-2}\), with coefficient zero at \(m=3\). Included symbolic code reproduces weighted and unweighted polynomial identities exactly; independent finite-graph brute tests and 99 transfer comparisons corroborate. No finite experiment establishes the infinite theorem.

originality.rationale: The complete all-circumference \(n\equiv2\pmod4\) ground-state counting and magnetization profile were not found in the inspected literature. Jacobsen–Salas (2013) supply a zero-field Ising/Potts partition-function transfer method; it encodes total counts algorithmically but does not give magnetization sectors or the evaluated formulas. Strečka, Karlová and Madaras (2015) give the specific \(n=10\) dodecahedral ground-state multiplicities \(250\), \(240\) at \(M=0\), and \(5\) each at \(M=\pm4\); this known case is credited and not claimed original. Sehrawat–Bhattacharjya (2019) optimize frustration over signings instead of counting fixed-signing magnetization sectors. An already established \(4\mid n\) Lucas law is explicitly outside the claim. Historical priority of the unbounded family remains a risk.
residual_risks: An unlocated specialized all-circumference maximum-cut or magnetization census could still imply the general law.
The 2013 unweighted Potts partition function is broad enough to encode total ground-state counts; the magnetization-refined theorem is not implied without adding a fugacity.
The n=10 instance was published in 2015; claiming its 250 and 240/5/5 values as novel would be incorrect, so they are used only as a consistency benchmark.
No independent audit or historical priority certification has been performed.

value.rationale: For \(GP(4r+2,2)\), two odd inner rings force an additional unsatisfied edge, producing a motivated structural parity boundary from the even-inner-ring situation. The theorem gives an exact infinite-family maximum-cut count and an unexpected universal restriction to ground-state magnetizations \(M\in\{0,\pm4\}\), with explicit Fibonacci-convolution multiplicities of the nonzero sectors. This extends, while crediting rather than re-claiming, the known \(n=10\) dodecahedral magnetic response; it is valuable for frustrated spin models and exact cubic-graph extremal enumeration.
